summary: Discover effective strategies for Climate-Resilient WASH in rural areas. Enroll in our training program to empower communities and ensure sustainable practices
lede: Climate-resilient WASH in rural communities connects climate risk screening, service vulnerability assessment, adaptation planning, and monitoring to help keep water, sanitation, and hygiene services functional during drought, floods, and changing conditions. This course uses the GWP-UNICEF Strategic Framework for WASH Climate Resilience and practical risk assessment methods to build those capabilities in a structured way. You will develop rural WASH risk profiles, assess and compare adaptation options, plan community engagement, and create maintenance checklists and resilience action plans. The course also introduces climate financing and donor reporting at overview level, helping you turn incomplete information, competing priorities, and limited budgets into practical decisions, implementation roadmaps, and reporting outputs.
audienceIntro: This course is intended for professionals who already work with rural water supply, sanitation, hygiene, or climate adaptation and need stronger decision tools for climate-resilient WASH in rural communities.
audience: Development Partners and Donor Programme Officers
prerequisites: You should bring a laptop, spreadsheet software, and familiarity with rural WASH operations, climate adaptation, or community-based service delivery. If available, bring an existing WASH project brief, service mapping data, or climate hazard information to use in exercises.
topics: Water & wastewater treatment and utility management
